components.note: A tall, intricate structure whose original picture (often read as a person leaning on a staff, uncertain which way to go) is debated; best learned as a whole.

example.hanzi: 我怀疑他说的不是真话。
example.pinyin: Wǒ huáiyí tā shuō de bú shì zhēnhuà.
example.english: I suspect that what he said isn't true.
example.fact: 疑 sits in 怀疑 (to doubt), 疑问 (question), 疑惑 (puzzled), 可疑 (suspicious) and 半信半疑 (half believing, half doubting). 疑 is mostly in compounds rather than alone.

components.note: 叒 (stacked hands or leaves) — the picking of leaves
木 (tree) — the mulberry tree

example.pinyin: Cán chī sāngyè.
example.english: Silkworms eat mulberry leaves.
example.fact: Mulberry leaves feed silkworms, which is why 桑 is tied to China's silk industry. 沧海桑田 ('blue seas turn to mulberry fields') is an idiom for great change, and 桑拿 is the loanword for sauna.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — forms the outer frame of the character

example.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ yuè lái yuè shuāiruò.
example.english: His health is getting weaker and weaker.
example.fact: 衰 has the readings shuāi (decline) and cuī (mourning garments). It appears in 衰老 (age), 衰退 (recession) and 衰弱 (feeble).

components.note: 艹 (grass) — a plant
西 (xī) gives the sound for one of its readings

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng rǎnliào láizì qiàncǎo.
example.english: This dye comes from madder.
example.fact: 茜草 (madder) was one of the oldest red dyes in China. 茜 is also a popular girls' name, read xī in some cases such as 茜茜.

excludeSuggestion: rare outside names and the word 茜草

components.note: 贝 (shell) — money and trade
覀 (cover) — a roof storing goods; a loose hint

example.pinyin: Jiǎ lǎoshī jiāo wǒmen shùxué.
example.english: Teacher Jia teaches us maths.
example.fact: 贾 is a surname read Jiǎ; the 'merchant' sense is gǔ, as in 商贾. In Dream of the Red Chamber, the 贾 family and 贾雨村 sound like 假 ('false'), a pun.

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort
艹 (top) — replaces the doubled flames of the older form 勞, toil by lamplight

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān xīnqín láodòng.
example.english: He works hard every day.
example.fact: 劳 gives 劳动 (labour), 劳驾 ('excuse me, may I trouble you'), 劳累 (weary) and 功劳 (merit). 五一劳动节 is May Day.

components.note: 知 (know) — knowledge; it also gives the sound
日 (sun) — brightness, clarity

example.hanzi: 他是一个很有智慧的人。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè hěn yǒu zhìhuì de rén.
example.english: He is a very wise person.
example.fact: 智 is in 智慧 (wisdom), 智商 (IQ), 智能 (smart, as in 智能手机 'smartphone') and 人工智能 (artificial intelligence).

components.note: 亻 (person) — a debtor
责 (zé, duty) — an obligation; it also gives a rough sound

example.pinyin: Tā hái qiàn yínháng hěn duō zhài.
example.english: He still owes the bank a lot of debt.
example.fact: 债 is colloquial in 欠债 (owe), 还债 (repay), and 债主 (creditor). 人情债 means a 'debt of gratitude'.

components.note: 彡 (hair) — facial hair
页 (head) — the face

example.pinyin: Chéngkè xū jì hǎo ānquándài.
example.english: Passengers must fasten their seat belts.
example.fact: 须 is formal: 必须 (must), 须知 (notice), 无须 (no need). In a different sense, it means a beard: 胡须. Compare 需 (xū, to need).

components.note: 纟 (silk thread) — threads and order
己 (jǐ) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā de niánjì bǐ wǒ dà.
example.english: He is older than me.
example.fact: 纪 sits in 年纪 (age), 世纪 (century), 纪律 (discipline), 纪念 (commemorate) and 纪录片 (documentary). As a surname it is read Jǐ.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire and explosions
包 (bāo) gives the sound — close to pào

example.hanzi: 过年的时候我们放鞭炮。
example.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou wǒmen fàng biānpào.
example.english: At New Year we set off firecrackers.
example.fact: 炮 gives 鞭炮 (firecrackers), 大炮 (cannon) and 炮弹 (shell). Firecrackers were traditionally lit to scare off evil spirits. The other readings, páo and bāo, are used in cooking.

components.note: 鱼 (fish) — sea creatures
包 (bāo) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā diǎn le yí fèn bàoyú.
example.english: He ordered a dish of abalone.
example.fact: 鲍鱼 is abalone, a prized banquet seafood. In classical writing 鲍鱼 referred to smelly salted fish, a different dish. 鲍 is also a surname.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — a metal tool
居 (jū) gives the sound — differs in tone

example.pinyin: Tā yòng jùzi jù mùtou.
example.english: He is sawing wood with a saw.
example.fact: 锯 is both the noun and the verb. 锯齿 (sawtooth), 电锯 (chainsaw) and 拉锯战 ('sawing battle', a seesaw struggle) all use it.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — addiction as an ailment
隐 (yǐn) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Tā chōuyān shàngyǐn le.
example.english: He became addicted to smoking.
example.fact: 瘾 appears in 上瘾 (get hooked), 烟瘾 (nicotine craving), 网瘾 (internet addiction) and 过瘾 ('so satisfying', as in a craving scratched).

components.note: 贝 (shell) — money paid
卖 (mài) offers a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 他想把抵押的房子赎回来。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bǎ dǐyā de fángzi shú huílái.
example.english: He wants to redeem the mortgaged house.
example.fact: 赎 is found in 赎回 (buy back), 赎罪 (atone) and 救赎 (redemption; the film The Shawshank Redemption is 肖申克的救赎).

components.note: 田 (field) — farmland, with a paw print above it in the early form

example.pinyin: Tā xià le yì fān gōngfu.
example.english: He put in a good deal of effort.
example.fact: 番 is a measure word for efforts and occasions: 一番话, 三番五次 (repeatedly). It originally meant 'foreign', as in 番茄 (tomato) and 番薯 (sweet potato).

components.note: 米 (rice) — grains
立 (lì) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Tā wǎn lǐ shèng le jǐ lì mǐfàn.
example.english: A few grains of rice are left in his bowl.
example.fact: 粒 is a measure word for small round things: 一粒米, 一粒糖, 一粒药. It's in 颗粒 (granule) and 粒子 (particle in physics).

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — hollow bamboo
同 (tóng) gives the sound — a near match

example.hanzi: 他把画卷起来放进纸筒里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ huà juǎn qǐlái fàng jìn zhǐtǒng lǐ.
example.english: He rolled up the painting and put it in a paper tube.
example.fact: 筒 appears in 笔筒 (pen holder), 垃圾筒 (trash can), 手电筒 (flashlight). It originally meant a piece of bamboo tube.

components.note: 门 (gate) — an entrance
木 (wood) — a wooden bar across it, the older sense of barrier

example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ hěn xián.
example.english: I'm free this weekend.
example.fact: 闲 means being idle or having nothing to do: 闲聊 (chat), 悠闲 (leisurely), 闲逛 (stroll). 有空 is a more neutral way to say you're free.

components.note: 爫 (hand) — a hand reaching
木 (tree) — picking fruit or leaves

example.pinyin: Wǒmen qù shān shang cǎi mógu.
example.english: We're going up the mountain to pick mushrooms.
example.fact: 采 gives 采访 (interview), 采用 (adopt), 采购 (purchase). Don't confuse it with 彩 (colour) or 踩 (to step on).

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person
加 (jiā) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang liàn yújiā.
example.english: She does yoga every morning.
example.fact: 伽 is used in transliterations, such as 瑜伽 (yoga) and 伽利略 (Galileo). In 伽马 (gamma) it reads gā and in 伽蓝 (monastery) qié.

components.note: Simplified from 實, a roof 宀 over strings of coins, picturing a house full of goods and hence something solid.

example.pinyin: Tā shì gè hěn lǎoshi de rén.
example.english: He is a very honest person.
example.fact: 实 gives 老实 (honest), 事实 (fact), 实现 (achieve), 现实 (reality), 实习 (internship) and 其实 (actually). It can also mean 'fruit' in 果实.

components.note: A tall building with a roof built on a raised mound.

example.pinyin: Tā qùnián bān dào le Běijīng.
example.english: He moved to Beijing last year.
example.fact: 京 means 'capital': 北京 (northern capital), 南京 (southern capital), 东京 (Tokyo, 'eastern capital') and 京剧 (Peking opera).

components.note: 亻 (person) — a soldier
丈 (zhàng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Tāmen dǎ le yì chǎng dà zhàng.
example.english: They fought a major battle.
example.fact: 仗 means a battle: 打仗 (to fight a war), 胜仗 (a victory). It also means to rely on, as in 仗义 (loyal to friends) and 仗势欺人 (to bully using one's power).

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — a garment
末 (mò) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Wǒ de wàzi pò le.
example.english: My sock has a hole.
example.fact: The measure word for socks is 双: 一双袜子. 丝袜 means silk stockings. 袜 usually appears as 袜子.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — a metal hook
勾 (gōu) — hooking; it also gives the sound

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ wàitào guà zài gōuzi shang.
example.english: He hung his coat on the hook.
example.fact: 钩 is a hook: 鱼钩 (fish hook), 钩针 (crochet needle). 打钩 means to tick a box with ✓.

components.note: Built from 甘 (sweet) over 匹; the original picture is uncertain, and the sense 'very, extreme' is the one that survives.

example.hanzi: 他甚至忘了自己的名字。
example.pinyin: Tā shènzhì wàng le zìjǐ de míngzi.
example.english: He even forgot his own name.
example.fact: 甚 is literary for 'very': 甚好, 不甚了解. In everyday text it is mostly seen in 甚至 (even), a very common linking word.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings
秋 (qiū) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā wèi qián de shì fāchóu.
example.english: She is worried about money.
example.fact: 愁 gives 发愁 (to worry), 愁眉苦脸 (a gloomy face) and 乡愁 (homesickness). Poetry links autumn (秋) with melancholy, which fits the 秋 (autumn) inside this character.

components.note: 石 (stone) — hard objects colliding
盍 (hé) offers a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Wǒ de tóu kē dào zhuōzi shang le.
example.english: I bumped my head on the table.
example.fact: 磕 is colloquial: 磕头 (kowtow), 磕磕绊绊 (stumbling), 磕巴 (stammer). In the north, 磕瓜子 means cracking sunflower seeds with the teeth.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — a razor
弟 (dì) gives the sound — differs in tone

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ húzi tì diào le.
example.english: He shaved off his beard.
example.fact: 剃 appears in 剃头 (to shave the head) and 剃须刀 (razor). The Qing 剃发令 of 1645 forced men to shave their foreheads and wear a queue.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings
敝 (bì) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā biē le yí dùzi qì.
example.english: He's bottled up a lot of anger.
example.fact: 憋 is colloquial: 憋气 (hold one's breath), 憋尿 (hold in urine) and 憋屈 (feel wronged). It has the meaning of something held in with no outlet.

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquid sap
桼 (qī) gives the sound — an exact match; it pictures a tree dripping sap

example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bǎ mén qī chéng hóngsè.
example.english: He wants to paint the door red.
example.fact: 漆 is lacquer from the sap of the lacquer tree, used in China for thousands of years (漆器). 油漆 is paint, and 漆黑 means pitch black.

components.note: 欠 (a yawning mouth) — breath and emotion
又 stands in for the older sound part 雚 (guàn) — a loose hint

example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan zhè shǒu gē.
example.english: I really like this song.
example.fact: 欢 appears in 喜欢 (like), 欢迎 (welcome), 欢乐 (joy), 欢呼 (cheer). In 喜欢 it takes a neutral tone.

components.note: 爫 (hand) — a hand placed above
女 (woman) — traditionally read as calming someone, 'settled'

example.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ hěn tuǒdang.
example.english: This method is very suitable.
example.fact: 妥 gives 妥当 (proper), 妥协 (compromise), 妥善 (appropriate), 稳妥 (safe). 办妥 means to have settled something.

components.note: 父 (father) — a father
多 (duō) offers a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Wǒ diē jīnnián liùshí suì le.
example.english: My dad is sixty this year.
example.fact: 爹 is a colloquial, often dialect word for 'dad', and 爸 is the standard form. 爹妈 means 'mum and dad', and 坑爹 is slang for something outrageous.

components.note: 土 (earth) — earthen walls and ground giving way

example.pinyin: Fángzi bèi dàxuě yā tā le.
example.english: The house collapsed under the heavy snow.
example.fact: 塌 gives 倒塌 (collapse), 塌方 (landslide), 塌陷 (cave-in) and 塌实 (at ease, also written 踏实). 塌房 became slang for a celebrity's reputation collapsing.

components.note: 页 (head) — thinking ahead
予 (yǔ) gives the sound — a near match

example.hanzi: 我想提前预订一个房间。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tíqián yùdìng yí gè fángjiān.
example.english: I'd like to reserve a room in advance.
example.fact: 预 gives 预订 (book), 预习 (prepare lessons), 预报 (forecast), 预防 (prevent), 预算 (budget).

components.note: 王 (jade) — gems
俞 (yú) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò qù shàng yújiā kè.
example.english: I go to a yoga class on weekends.
example.fact: 瑜 originally means beautiful jade: 瑕不掩瑜 ('a flaw doesn't hide the jade's luster'). It's also in 瑜伽 (yoga) and in names such as 周瑜.

components.note: 木 (tree) — plants
直 (zhí) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Chūntiān wǒmen yìqǐ zhíshù.
example.english: In spring we plant trees together.
example.fact: 植 gives 植物 (plant), 植树节 (Arbor Day, 12 March in China), 移植 (transplant) and 种植 (cultivate).

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — an injury
巴 (bā) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Tā liǎn shang yǒu yí dào bā.
example.english: He has a scar on his face.
example.fact: The measure word is 道: 一道疤. 伤疤 means scar, 揭伤疤 means 'to pick at an old wound', and 好了伤疤忘了疼 means to forget pain once healed.

components.note: 木 (wood) — the old sense was a wooden crossbar
黄 (huáng) gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ xiāngzi héng zhe fàng.
example.english: He placed the box sideways.
example.fact: 横 is the opposite of 竖. It's also the first stroke 一 in writing. 横 read hèng means fierce, as in 蛮横 (unreasonable).

components.note: 忄 (heart) — disposition
赖 (lài) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā hěn lǎn, bú ài zuò jiāwù.
example.english: He's lazy and dislikes housework.
example.fact: 懒 gives 偷懒 (slack off), 懒得 (can't be bothered: 懒得说), and 睡懒觉 (sleep in).

components.note: 氵 (water) — rushing water
敫 (jiǎo) offers a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 这个消息让大家很激动。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi ràng dàjiā hěn jīdòng.
example.english: This news got everyone excited.
example.fact: 激 gives 激动 (excited or moved), 刺激 (stimulate), 激烈 (fierce), 激光 (laser), 感激 (grateful). 激动 can be positive or angry.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a bewitching figure
夭 (yāo) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ yǒu yì zhī húli yāo.
example.english: There's a fox demon in the story.
example.fact: 妖 gives 妖怪 (monster), 妖精 (spirit), and also means bewitching (妖艳). Folk tales about 狐妖 are classic.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — tying
困 (kùn) gives the sound — a near match

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ shū kǔn chéng yì kǔn.
example.english: He tied the books into a bundle.
example.fact: 捆 is both a verb and a measure word: 一捆柴 (a bundle of firewood). 捆绑销售 means bundled sales.

components.note: 女 (woman) — matchmaking in the old sense
某 (mǒu) offers a loose sound hint

example.hanzi: 现在人们通过社交媒体联系。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài rénmen tōngguò shèjiāo méitǐ liánxì.
example.english: Nowadays people stay in touch through social media.
example.fact: 媒 originally meant matchmaker (媒人). It later extended to 'medium': 媒体 (media), 传媒, 媒介.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — prying
毳 (cuì) offers a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu qiào kāi le chuānghu.
example.english: The thief pried the window open.
example.fact: 撬 gives 撬锁 (pick a lock), 撬棍 (crowbar) and 撬墙脚 (to poach a partner or employee).

components.note: 攵 (strike) — conflict
舌 stands in for the older 啇 (dí) — a sound hint

example.pinyin: Wǒmen bù néng qīngdí.
example.english: We can't underestimate the enemy.
example.fact: 敌 gives 敌人 (enemy), 敌意 (hostility), 无敌 (invincible), 轻敌 (underestimate) and 情敌 (love rival).

components.note: 风 (wind) — a gale
猋 (biāo) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Tā kāichē biāo dào le yì bǎi bā.
example.english: He drove up to 180.
example.fact: 飙 is slang: 飙车 (street racing), 飙升 (skyrocket), 飙泪 (burst into tears). Originally it meant a violent wind.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — moving away
辟 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhǎo le gè dìfang bì yǔ.
example.english: We found a place to shelter from the rain.
example.fact: 避 gives 避免 (avoid), 避开 (steer clear of), 逃避 (escape), 避孕 (contraception), 避暑 (escape the heat).
